why: Both engineers found the single chokepoint (ChatModelManager) and moved the same OpenAI/Anthropic traffic with behaviour intact, so the migrations are near-equivalent — but A also wrapped ChatOpenRouter's inner client, which B's own validator flagged as unrouted. On the part that matters most, A delivered a real CTO-level review with four built, tested, live-measured improvements (feature labels, prompt caching at -73% input, cheap-model background summarization at 48x, deleting a whole round trip) plus a credible rework and the who-pays decision, while B shipped one proposed improvement, no caching, no model-tier thinking, and rejected the Flex discount on a fear A actually measured and disproved (same median latency, half the price).
A_best: It questioned whether each call should exist and at what price, then proved the answers live: a 9,158-token prefix caching 8,960 tokens only once a prompt_cache_key exists, compaction at $0.0927 → $0.0019 on a same-vendor cheap model, condensation removed entirely because the prompt and the tool schema both say the history is usually empty — each with a named loss and a reason keys were omitted where the prefix doesn't repeat.
B_best: The honest, product-grounded reason for pinning service_tier "default" — a chat pane the user is reading — backed by a test that drives the real production path (createModelInstanceFromBridged → ChatOpenAI → wrapped fetch) and asserts the exact outgoing URL and body shape with and without the Router key, which is stronger migration evidence than a replayed curl.
A_worst: Evidence hygiene: it reports the full suite green while the outside check still shows tests "running" against a baseline with a failure, 7 of 12 routes are unverified, and the report is truncated mid-item (i6) — and even at its best it never reaches spend caps, shadow models, Jev or Switchyard as named levers.
B_worst: The system-level judgment is a migration tune-up, not a redesign: it names caching as "reviewed" and then does nothing about a large fixed system prefix, leaves the only improvement unbuilt, dismisses fallbacks without considering same-vendor cheaper candidates for background calls, and misreads chainUtils.ts as "inline-edit / note rewriting" when it is follow-up question condensation — the one call A showed can often be skipped outright.
